---

## Critical

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-21_v0.10.0/T1__leveraged__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:16`** - SQL injection via f-string query construction

What: `user_id` is taken directly from `request.query` and interpolated into an SQL string with an f-string. Any value such as `' OR '1'='1` will alter the query's semantics. The existing `is_valid_id` helper in `service/validator.py` exists precisely to guard against this but is never called here.

Why: This allows an attacker to bypass the `WHERE id = ...` clause and read arbitrary rows (or, depending on the SQLite configuration, perform other destructive operations) without any valid credentials beyond the `Authorization` header.

Suggested direction: Replace the f-string with a parameterised query using the DB-API `?` placeholder — `"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?"` with `(user_id,)` as the second argument to `_DB.execute`. Also call `is_valid_id(user_id)` before executing and return a 400 if it fails, which is consistent with the validator already being present in the codebase.

---

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-21_v0.10.0/T1__leveraged__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:14`** - Missing validation of absent `id` query parameter

What: `request.query.get("id")` returns `None` when the parameter is not supplied. `user_id` is then `None`, and the f-string on line 16 produces `WHERE id = 'None'` — a string comparison against the literal text `"None"` rather than a proper missing-parameter error.

Why: This silently produces a 404 instead of a 400 (bad request), which is semantically wrong and could mask integration bugs in callers. `is_valid_id` already handles `None` correctly by returning `False`, so the guard is already written.

Suggested direction: Check `user_id` with `is_valid_id` immediately after line 14 and return `{"status": 400, "body": {"error": "invalid id"}}` when it fails. This handles both the `None` case and malformed input in one place.

---

## Important

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-21_v0.10.0/T1__leveraged__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:7`** - Module-level shared mutable SQLite connection

What: `_DB = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")` is created once at import time as a module-level global. SQLite connections are not thread-safe by default (`check_same_thread=True` is the default). Any concurrent requests will race on this single connection object.

Why: In a multi-threaded or async serving environment this will raise `ProgrammingError: SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread`, or cause silent data corruption if `check_same_thread=False` is set without a lock.

Suggested direction: Either pass `check_same_thread=False` and guard every access with a `threading.Lock`, use a connection pool, or move connection creation into a per-request context. The in-memory store is presumably for development only; flag this with a comment if it is intentional.

---

## Nice to have

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-21_v0.10.0/T1__leveraged__r1/work/tests/test_users.py:7`** - Missing coverage for the no-`id` and invalid-`id` cases

What: The test suite covers the happy path (known user) and the auth guard, but there is no test for a missing `id` parameter, an invalid/malformed `id`, or an unknown-but-valid `id` (expected 404).

Why: The two critical bugs above would have been caught by a missing-`id` test. Adding these cases would lock in the correct 400/404 behaviour after the fixes are applied.

Suggested direction: Add test cases mirroring `_Req(auth="Bearer test", qid=None)` (expect 400), `_Req(auth="Bearer test", qid="' OR '1'='1")` (expect 400), and `_Req(auth="Bearer test", qid="999")` (expect 404). This follows the same `_Req` pattern already used in the file.
